query: How does Work Queue ACK (Acknowledgement) work
answer:
**How does Work Queue ACK (Acknowledgement) work?**

Tetherfi Work Queue “ACK” feature ensures that a work item is delivered to the TMAC/Agent Desktop UI without fail. When a new item is added to queue, the item is removed from the queue only after the item is routed to the TMAC/AD UI and WQ receives and ACK from the UI.  EMM, TComm adds item to work queue.  In workqueue template.config there are two configs  <add key="AcknowledgementRequired" value="1"/>  <add key="WorkItemTTL" value="15000"/>  If “AcknowledgementRequired” is set to 1, then WQ will add items to queue with ACK enabled.  And the “WorkItemTTL” is the time in milliseconds WQ waits for an acknowledgment from the UI.  If this “WorkItemTTL” is not set or set to 0, then WQ will use the default value “20000” (20 seconds).  After WQ adds the items to queue with ACK enabled, and when the TMAC server receives this WQ item, TMAC server adds a ACK section to the interaction construct event (TextChatIncomingEvent, IncomingEmailEvent)  "ACK": { "IsRequired": true, "Source": "workqueue", "Id": "dev210930234153_2618", "Channel": "TextChat" }, When the TMAC JS SDK receives this interaction construct event, the SDK checks for this “ACK” property and if the “IsRequired” parameter is set to “true”, the SDK calls TMAC proxy method “EventAcknowledgement” method.TMAC SDK proxy forwards this method to TMAC Server.  When the TMAC JS SDK receives this interaction construct event, the SDK checks for this “ACK” property and if the “IsRequired” parameter is set to “true”, the SDK calls TMAC proxy method “EventAcknowledgement” method.TMAC SDK proxy forwards this method to TMAC Server.    public static CommandResultEvent EventAcknowledgement(string agentId, string channel, string itemId, string source)  agentId – id of the agent who received the event  channel – interaction channel  itemId – session id of the item  source – workqueue    If the source it “workqueue”, then TMAC will forward this method to WQ server.  The WQ will wait for the number of milliseconds configured in “WorkItemTTL”. If the ACK comes before the TTL the item is removed from the queue, else the item will remain in the queue and it will be routed to next agent.

**How does the TMAC to IVR transfer for TPIN/OTP works?**

When an agent receives an incoming call from a customer or makes an outbound call to the customer using Agent Desktop or TMAC UI, sometimes agents are required to collect some secure data from the customer to authenticate the customer. Some of these data might be personal data that cannot be shared with an agent (such as telephone pin, NRIC ID).  In such a scenario, the agent can transfer the customer to an IVR flow that collects these secure data and authenticate the customer within the IVR without involving the agent.  TMAC (Agent Desktop and TMAC UI) provides an "IVR Transfer" feature for agents to transfer an incoming or outbound call to an IVR VDN. The most common two IVR transfers are TPIN transfer (IVR authenticates the user with a telephone pin) or OTP transfer (IVR authenticates the user with OTP sent to mobile).  In TMAC UI/Agent Desktop UI, there is a list of IVR transfer endpoints that can be configured using the Agent Desktop JSON. See below sample AD JSON:  "IVR": { "MenuEnabled": true, "DefaultMenu": [ "Main Menu", "Products", "Mobile", "Agent" ], "Transfer": { "Allowed": true, "Menu": [ { "Text": "Accesscode+TPIN", "Type": "v_nv", "Value": "tpin", "Icon": "lock" } ] } }, When the agent clicks the IVR transfer option in the IVR transfer menu, AD/TMACUI calls the TMAC server "TransferToIvr" method with the "value" in above Menu ("tpin" in this example).  When transferring a call to IVR, there are two different modes.  Agent Trasnfer the call to IVR and move to next call  Agent Trasnfer the call to IVR and waits for IVR to send the call back to agent (for TPIN/OTP authentication calls) - this is called "transfer with aux"  For TMAC server to identify the mode of transfer, there is a configuration in TMAC server template.conig called "Voice_IVRTransferTypesRequiresAux". This config contains a comma separated list of "values" which would be considered as mode #2 (transfer and wait for the call to come back to agent).  sample:  <add key="Voice_IVRTransferTypesRequiresAux" value="tpin,opt,vb" />  First TMAC identified the mode of transfer.  Then TMAC server tries to get a record from "AGT_IVR_Transfer_VDNs" table based on the provided "value". The DB record returns a "VDN".  For mode #1 above, TMAC does a blind transfer to IVR VDN. And the agent can close the tab and move to next call.  For mode #2 above, TMAC has to perform several actions.  First TMAC will get the VDN number from the above table.  Then TMAC server prepares the transfer UUI based on the uui.config. For IVR Transfers with AUX enabled, the UUI should contain the "AgentId", "InteractionID" and the "Original VDN" of the call. These values are injected to UUI based on the "uui.config" file inside TMAC server folder.  (Latest version of TMAC server >= 5.1.4.15 can inject the original UCID also to the transfer UUI).  Once the UUI is prepared, then TMAC server tries to find a AUX code matching to the transfer "value" (ex: tpin). These values are configured in DB table "AGT_AUX_Codes" (with value=tpin in this example).  If the aux code is found, then TMAC server first changes the agent state to that aux. If aux code was not found then AUX-0 will be used as default.  Since the agent is still on-call, the state will goto a "pending" state and wait for the call to get dropped from agent station.  After changing the the agent state to "pending-aux", then TMAC server performs a "Blind Transfer" to IVR VDN with the updated UUI.  If the blind transfer is successful, then TMAC server immedialty starts a wait timer which will wait for number of seconds configured in TMAC server template.config "TransferAUXTime" value. Usually this value should be greater than the time it might take for customer to complete the IVR flow and connect back to agent. If the this wait timer times out before the IVR send the call back to agent, then a event "AUXTimerEvent" is send to AD/TMAC UI.  Also, the agent will be pushed to the AUX state which was configured in "AGT_AUX_Codes".  Now the IVR starts promoting the user to enter the details for authentication. IVR may use the "Original VDN" number (and/or the Original UCID) entered in the UUI from TMAC serer before blind transfer to decide the IVR flow.  Meantime the agent waits for the call to come back from IVR.  Once the IVR completes the processing of the call, IVR has to send the call back to agent. To identify the agent, IVR uses the UUI's AgentID data section. And then IVR does a blind transfer back to "agent id" with updated UUI with new authentication status/data. The UUI may have the agentid and the interaction ID as well (in some IVR implementations, these data can be wiped out before the call is sent back to agent).  When the IVR transfers the call back to "agent id", the call will comes to agent's phone but it will start rining based on the "DAC - direct agent calling" settings configured in the Avaya CM. Based on this DAC settings, the call will be offered to agent's phone. Since the agent is on "AUX" state, and the IVR transfers the call to "agent id" (not the station id), the call is considered as a ACD call (based on DAC settings). If the agent is in on AUX when call comes to the phone, the phone will park the call and show an indicator to agent. Then the agent has to goto "Available" state to receive the call on AD/TMAC.  Or (based on DAC settings), the agent might get the call directly on AD/TMAC UI without getting parked on the phone.  Either way, when the TMAC server gets the new call, it first checks the UUI for agent id and the interaction ID based on "uui.config".  If the "interaction ID" is found in the UUI, then TMAC looks for the same interaction in agent session. If the Interaction is found (which means the agent has not closed the interaction yet), then TMAC does not create a new interaction. Instead it used the same interaction and send an "IncomingCallUpdateEvent" to the AD/TMAC UI (other events such as UUI data, IVR data also will be processed subsequently). In the AD/TMAC UI the existing interaction tab will be updated with new data.  If the Interaction ID is not found in UUI or the interaction ID is not found in agent session, then a new interaction is created and agent will get the call in a new UI interaction tab (AD/TMAC UI).

query: How does component licensing or TMAC server work
answer:
**How does TMAC server or any other component licensing work?**

TMAC server has three different licensing modes:  Instance License  Evaluation License  Developer License  Instance License  An instance License is the preferred type of license for the TMAC server. The license is generated by the Tetherfi product team for a provided MAC address of a server. The request to generate the license has to be sent to the product team (there is a designated email address for this) along with required details (customer details, MAC address of the server).  The product team will create the license file and share it with the implementation team. The license comes in a form of a “.lic” file which has to be placed in the Tetherfi License Server folder.  After placing the license file into the Tetherfi License Server/Manager, the Licence server has to be restarted. The Licence server can successfully start only if the license is valid.  During the server startup, the TMAC server tries to connect to licensing server to acquire a valid license. If the license server is not present or if it is stopped (due to an invalid license), the TMAC server will not be able to acquire the license and the TMAC will fallback to next licensing mode (Evaluation License).    TMAC connects to the License server's WCF (HTTP) interface using "TetherfiLicClient.dll". The DLL should match the License Server version.  Below configuration is used in TMAC server to configure license server url:  <system.serviceModel> <client> <endpoint address="http://localhost/LicenseServer/" binding="basicHttpBinding" bindingConfiguration="basicHttp" contract="TetherfiLicenseServer.ITetherfiLicService" name="LicenseServer1" /> </client> </system.serviceModel> Evaluation License  The Evaluation license mode can be used for demo and POC purposes. It is not recommended to be used in SIT/UAT/Production systems.  The evaluation license can be generated for TMAC server by the product development team. To generate an eval license, you have to provide the MAC address, IP address, and the expiry date requirement to the product team. Based on the provided data, the product team can generate an evaluation license Key and share it.  The generated evaluation license key has to be placed in template.config file of the TMAC server.  <add key="EvalLicenseKey" value="place your key here" /> And the IP of the server (which was provided to product team) should be configured in below:  <add key="EvalLicenseLocalIP" value="10.1.1.10" /> This IP should be a valid IP assigned to any of the network interfaces of the server. If there is an IP change, then you must get a new eval license key.  The evaluation license takes the second precedence during TMAC server start-up. If the TMAC server was not able to acquire the license from the License Manager/Server, then it looks for an evaluation license in the above “EvalLicenseKey”. The key is then extracted to get the MAC ID, IP, and the expiry date of the key. And these data is then validated against the current server’s MAC ID, IP, and the system date time.  If all the validations are passed, then TMAC server will start successfully, else TMAC will fallback to the next licensing mode (Developer license).  Developer License  The developer license is generally used during the development and testing teams only. Using the development license mode, TMAC can be started without a License Server or an evaluation license. This gives the flexibility to the developers to run the TMAC server in any environment.  The developer license can be configured in the below key in TMAC server template.config.  <add key="Developer" value="Add the developer license key here" /> Number of agent sessions allowed: The license returned from License server has a property called "MaxAgentsAllowed" and TMAC will allow that many agent sessions to be created per TMAC server instance. If there is no license server used, then TMAC will use the config "AgentSession_MaxAgentsAllowed" to determine the max number of sessions allowed per TMAC server.

query: How does component licensing or TMAC server work
answer:
**How does TMAC server or any other component licensing work?**

TMAC server has three different licensing modes:  Instance License  Evaluation License  Developer License  Instance License  An instance License is the preferred type of license for the TMAC server. The license is generated by the Tetherfi product team for a provided MAC address of a server. The request to generate the license has to be sent to the product team (there is a designated email address for this) along with required details (customer details, MAC address of the server).  The product team will create the license file and share it with the implementation team. The license comes in a form of a “.lic” file which has to be placed in the Tetherfi License Server folder.  After placing the license file into the Tetherfi License Server/Manager, the Licence server has to be restarted. The Licence server can successfully start only if the license is valid.  During the server startup, the TMAC server tries to connect to licensing server to acquire a valid license. If the license server is not present or if it is stopped (due to an invalid license), the TMAC server will not be able to acquire the license and the TMAC will fallback to next licensing mode (Evaluation License).    TMAC connects to the License server's WCF (HTTP) interface using "TetherfiLicClient.dll". The DLL should match the License Server version.  Below configuration is used in TMAC server to configure license server url:  <system.serviceModel> <client> <endpoint address="http://localhost/LicenseServer/" binding="basicHttpBinding" bindingConfiguration="basicHttp" contract="TetherfiLicenseServer.ITetherfiLicService" name="LicenseServer1" /> </client> </system.serviceModel> Evaluation License  The Evaluation license mode can be used for demo and POC purposes. It is not recommended to be used in SIT/UAT/Production systems.  The evaluation license can be generated for TMAC server by the product development team. To generate an eval license, you have to provide the MAC address, IP address, and the expiry date requirement to the product team. Based on the provided data, the product team can generate an evaluation license Key and share it.  The generated evaluation license key has to be placed in template.config file of the TMAC server.  <add key="EvalLicenseKey" value="place your key here" /> And the IP of the server (which was provided to product team) should be configured in below:  <add key="EvalLicenseLocalIP" value="10.1.1.10" /> This IP should be a valid IP assigned to any of the network interfaces of the server. If there is an IP change, then you must get a new eval license key.  The evaluation license takes the second precedence during TMAC server start-up. If the TMAC server was not able to acquire the license from the License Manager/Server, then it looks for an evaluation license in the above “EvalLicenseKey”. The key is then extracted to get the MAC ID, IP, and the expiry date of the key. And these data is then validated against the current server’s MAC ID, IP, and the system date time.  If all the validations are passed, then TMAC server will start successfully, else TMAC will fallback to the next licensing mode (Developer license).  Developer License  The developer license is generally used during the development and testing teams only. Using the development license mode, TMAC can be started without a License Server or an evaluation license. This gives the flexibility to the developers to run the TMAC server in any environment.  The developer license can be configured in the below key in TMAC server template.config.  <add key="Developer" value="Add the developer license key here" /> Number of agent sessions allowed: The license returned from License server has a property called "MaxAgentsAllowed" and TMAC will allow that many agent sessions to be created per TMAC server instance. If there is no license server used, then TMAC will use the config "AgentSession_MaxAgentsAllowed" to determine the max number of sessions allowed per TMAC server.

query: How does Work Queue ACK  work
answer:
**How does Work Queue ACK (Acknowledgement) work?**

Tetherfi Work Queue “ACK” feature ensures that a work item is delivered to the TMAC/Agent Desktop UI without fail. When a new item is added to queue, the item is removed from the queue only after the item is routed to the TMAC/AD UI and WQ receives and ACK from the UI.  EMM, TComm adds item to work queue.  In workqueue template.config there are two configs  <add key="AcknowledgementRequired" value="1"/>  <add key="WorkItemTTL" value="15000"/>  If “AcknowledgementRequired” is set to 1, then WQ will add items to queue with ACK enabled.  And the “WorkItemTTL” is the time in milliseconds WQ waits for an acknowledgment from the UI.  If this “WorkItemTTL” is not set or set to 0, then WQ will use the default value “20000” (20 seconds).  After WQ adds the items to queue with ACK enabled, and when the TMAC server receives this WQ item, TMAC server adds a ACK section to the interaction construct event (TextChatIncomingEvent, IncomingEmailEvent)  "ACK": { "IsRequired": true, "Source": "workqueue", "Id": "dev210930234153_2618", "Channel": "TextChat" }, When the TMAC JS SDK receives this interaction construct event, the SDK checks for this “ACK” property and if the “IsRequired” parameter is set to “true”, the SDK calls TMAC proxy method “EventAcknowledgement” method.TMAC SDK proxy forwards this method to TMAC Server.  When the TMAC JS SDK receives this interaction construct event, the SDK checks for this “ACK” property and if the “IsRequired” parameter is set to “true”, the SDK calls TMAC proxy method “EventAcknowledgement” method.TMAC SDK proxy forwards this method to TMAC Server.    public static CommandResultEvent EventAcknowledgement(string agentId, string channel, string itemId, string source)  agentId – id of the agent who received the event  channel – interaction channel  itemId – session id of the item  source – workqueue    If the source it “workqueue”, then TMAC will forward this method to WQ server.  The WQ will wait for the number of milliseconds configured in “WorkItemTTL”. If the ACK comes before the TTL the item is removed from the queue, else the item will remain in the queue and it will be routed to next agent.

query: How does Work Queue ACK (Acknowledgement) work
answer:
The Work Queue ACK (Acknowledgement) feature ensures that a work item is delivered to the TMAC/Agent Desktop UI without fail. When a new item is added to the queue, it waits for an acknowledgment from the UI for a specified time (configured in milliseconds). If the acknowledgment is received before the time limit, the item is removed from the queue. If not, the item remains in the queue and is routed to the next agent.
